C: › [ C ] the long tube in the body of a person or animal, through which food moves during the process of digesting food
› [ C ] informal a person's stomach when it is extremely large

U: › [ U ] a strong thread made from an animal's bowels used, especially in the past, for making musical instruments and sports rackets
（尤指舊時用來製作樂器和球拍的）腸線

NONE: › a strong belief about someone or something that cannot completely be explained and does not have to be decided by reasoning
直覺，本能，內心感覺
› a way of deciding what should be done or what is right, that is based on how someone feels rather than thinking about reasons
憑直覺，憑感情（決定或判斷）
› courage in dealing with danger or uncertainty
勇氣，膽量，意志

T: › to destroy the inside of a building completely, usually by fire
（通常指火災）徹底損毀（房屋）的內部
› to remove the inside parts and contents of a building, usually so that it can be decorated in a completely new way
（通常指為了裝修）拆除（房屋）的內部
› to remove the inner organs of an animal, especially in preparation for eating it

example: Meat stays in the gut longer than vegetable matter.
和蔬菜相比，肉類在消化道中停留的時間更長。
He's got a huge beer gut (= large stomach caused by drinking beer).
他有個大啤酒肚。
My guts hurt.
我五臟六腑都痛。
He got a knife in the guts.
他肚子被戳了一刀。
I have a gut feeling that the relationship won't last.
我有種直覺，這段關係不會太長久。
My head said that I should go but my gut said I should stay.
理智上我該走，但是感覺告訴我該留。
I went with my gut and chose Sarah to lead the team.
我聽從了直覺，選擇莎拉領導隊伍。
[ + to infinitive ] It takes a lot of guts to admit to so many people that you've made a mistake.
在那麼多人面前承認自己犯了錯誤是需要很大勇氣的。
A fire gutted the bookshop last week.
上星期一場火把書店燒光了。
She gutted the fish and cut off their heads.
她取出魚的內臟並把魚頭切掉。

NONE: › making you feel very upset or worried
讓人覺得非常憤怒（或擔憂）的
› showing no courage
缺乏膽量的，窩囊的，沒有勇氣的

example: This government is too gutless to take on the big long-term problems such as pollution.
這個政府太窩囊，根本無法應對像治理污染這樣需要從長計議的重大問題。

NONE: › brave and determined
勇敢的，堅毅的，有決心的

example: a gutsy performance
勇敢的表現

NONE: › extremely disappointed and unhappy
非常沮喪的；非常失望的；極度傷心的

example: He was gutted when she finished the relationship.
她跟他分手後，他傷心欲絕。

C: › [ C ] the edge of a road where rain flows away
› [ C ] an open pipe, usually at the lower edge of a roof, that collects and carries away rain

NONE: › the lowest level, especially of society
（尤指社會的）最低層，貧民窟
› (of a flame or candle) to burn unevenly and weakly, especially before completely stopping burning
（火焰或蠟燭，尤指在熄滅前）忽明忽暗，搖曳不定

example: Born to a poverty-stricken family, she dragged herself out of the gutter to become a successful business owner.
她出生在一個極度貧困的家庭，但是她從社會最低層奮力掙扎出來，成功地擁有了自己的公司。
a guttering candle
搖曳不定的燭光

NONE: › offensive language
冒犯性語言
› the system of open pipes on a building that collects and carries away rain
（建築物外的）排水系統
› a child from a poor area of a town who is dirty and badly dressed
貧民區衣衫襤褸的髒孩子

example: a Victorian guttersnipe
維多利亞時期衣衫襤褸的窮孩子

NONE: › (of speech sounds) produced at the back of the throat and therefore deep
（話音）喉嚨裡發出的，粗嘎的

example: Two Egyptians were arguing outside the room, their voices loud and guttural.
兩個埃及人正在屋外扯著嗓門粗聲粗氣地爭吵。
